title_en: Huabu Economic and Trade Company v. China Sinotrans Shandong Weihai Company et al. — dispute over ship import agency contract and scrap steel vessel sales contract

full_text_en:
Huabu Economic and Trade Company v. China Ocean Shipping Agency Shandong Weihai Company et al.

— Dispute over Ship Import Agency Contract and Scrap Steel Ship Sale Contract

Promulgated by the Supreme People's Court (No. 33 of 2002)

CIVIL RULING OF THE SUPREME PEOPLE'S COURT

Retrial Case No. 3 (2000)

Applicant for Retrial (Original Appellee at First Instance): Dongning County Huabu Economic and Trade Company. Domicile: No. 19 Zhonghua Road, Dongning Town, Dongning County, Heilongjiang Province.

Legal Representative: Li Wenyi, Manager of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Hu Anchao, Attorney at Beijing Huayi Law Firm.

Original Appellant (Defendant at First Instance): China Ocean Shipping Agency Shandong Weihai Company (formerly Shandong Province Foreign Trade Transportation Branch Weihai Sub-branch). Domicile: No. 5 Qingdao North Road, Weihai City.

Legal Representative: Mu Dedi, General Manager of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Xu Shuze, Attorney at Shandong Zhengyuan Law Firm.
Long Bing, Deputy Manager of the Shipping Agency Department, China Ocean Shipping Agency Shandong Weihai Company.

Original Appellant (Defendant at First Instance): Weihai City Economic and Technological Development Zone Tengda Industrial Co., Ltd. (formerly Weihai City Economic and Technological Development Zone Timber Company). Domicile: Haopo Songjiawa, Weihai City Economic and Technological Development Zone.

Legal Representative: Wang Meihong (female), Manager of the Company.

Original Third Party: Yantai City Ship Scrapping Industry Company (formerly).

In the dispute over ship import agency contract and scrap steel ship sale contract between Dongning County Huabu Economic and Trade Company (hereinafter referred to as Huabu Company) and China Ocean Shipping Agency Shandong Weihai Company (hereinafter referred to as Weihai Overseas Shipping), Weihai Economic and Technological Development Zone Tengda Industrial Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as the former Timber Company), and the third party Yantai City Ship Scrapping Industry Company (hereinafter referred to as Ship Scrapping Company), the Shandong High People's Court rendered Civil Judgment No. 236 (1997) Luzhong Zhongzi on September 21, 1997, which has already taken legal effect. On October 31, 1997, the Judicial Committee of that court decided to retry the case, and on October 22, 1999, issued Ruling No. 167 (1997) Luzhong Zaizi: revoking Civil Judgment No. 236 (1997) Luzhong Zhongzi of that court and Civil Judgment No. 1 (1995) Qinghafa Haishi Chongzi of Qingdao Maritime Court; dismissing Huabu Company's lawsuit; and transferring the case to the public security authorities for handling. Huabu Company, dissatisfied with this ruling, filed an application for retrial with this court. On March 25, 2000, this court issued Civil Ruling No. 3 (2000) Jiaotizi, deciding to initiate a retrial of this case. After initiating the retrial, this court formed a collegial panel in accordance with the law, composed of Presiding Judge Lei Xuhui, Judge Wang Shumei, and Assistant Judge Li Qinghai, and held a public hearing of this case. Li Wenyi, the legal representative of Huabu Company, and his agent ad litem Hu Anchao, as well as agents ad litem Xu Shuze and Long Bing for Weihai Overseas Shipping, appeared in court for the proceedings. The legal representative of the former Timber Company, having been duly summoned without justifiable cause, failed to appear in court. The original third party, Ship Scrapping Company, had its business license revoked for failing to undergo the 1999 annual inspection and was legally cancelled by the Yantai Administration for Industry and Commerce on July 25, 2000, thus losing its capacity as a party to this litigation. This case has now been concluded.

The final judgment of the Shandong High People's Court at first instance found the following: On December 8, 1993, the Heilongjiang Province Border Trade Administration Bureau approved Huabu Company to entrust Dongning County Border Trade Company (hereinafter referred to as Border Trade Company) to conduct barter trade and economic and technological cooperation with the former Soviet Union and Eastern European countries through *Entrusted Agency Approval Certificate* No. 0220161-03864 HLDO-1206. On April 21, 1994, Huabu Company, in the name of Border Trade Company, signed two contracts with the Russian Nakhodka City South Coastal District Social Joint-Stock Company (hereinafter referred to as Russian Coastal District Company): one for the import of a scrap steel ship and steel rounds, and another for the export of canned beef. Both contracts bore the same number "HLDO-1206". The total value of each import and export contract was USD 328,000, with the scrap steel ship valued at USD 228,000. Both contracts were stamped for record by the Heilongjiang Province Border Trade Administration Bureau on April 26, 1994. The Dongning Customs Office of the People's Republic of China issued *Import/Export Goods Tax Reduction/Exemption Certificate* No. 940749 on April 27, 1994, approving a 50% reduction in customs duties on the scrap steel ship under barter trade.

On April 25, 1994, Huabu Company entered into an agreement with the former Timber Company stipulating that Huabu Company would import a scrap steel ship and sell it to the former Timber Company at a delivered duty-paid price of USD 146 per metric ton, totaling approximately 4,300 metric tons (based on the tonnage stated in the ship's documentation), amounting to USD 627,800. The former Timber Company was to pay a deposit of RMB 300,000 before April 29, make advance preparations for taking delivery of the ship, pay RMB 1,500,000 upon the ship's arrival at Dalian Port, complete the handover within three days, and pay the remaining balance within five days. On May 1, the scrap steel ship "NIKOLAI ISAENKO" (hereinafter referred to as the "Nikolai") arrived at Dalian Port. On May 5, the former Timber Company and Huabu Company entered into a supplementary agreement: at the former Timber Company's request, the ship was to be redirected to Weihai Port. After Huabu Company completed customs clearance, the former Timber Company was to take delivery immediately and pay the full ship price within five days. When Huabu Company asked the Russian party to sail the ship to Weihai Port for delivery, the Russian party demanded an advance payment of USD 100,000 in cash, failing which the ship would be sailed back to Russia. On the same day, Huabu Company entered into an agency contract with Weihai Overseas Shipping, entrusting Weihai Overseas Shipping to "act as ship agent and cargo agent to handle all import procedures for the 'Nikolai' ship." On May 17, the former Timber Company and the Russian Southern Sea Fishing Fleet Company Limited (hereinafter referred to as Russian Fleet Company) signed an agreement for the purchase and sale of the scrap steel ship "Nikolai," reselling it to the former Timber Company at USD 115 per metric ton, totaling USD 447,005; thereby terminating the scrap steel ship purchase and sale contract between the Russian party and Huabu Company. On the same day, the former Timber Company, Weihai Overseas Shipping, and the Russian crew onboard the "Nikolai" completed the ship handover procedures.

On June 1, 1994, the former Timber Company, in the name of Huabu Company, declared customs and paid customs duties of RMB 59,233.02 and import value-added tax of RMB 172,861.70 based on the 50% reduced duty rate approved by Dongning Customs for barter trade. On June 2, Weihai Customs released the "Nikolai." On June 8, the former Timber Company paid agency fees of RMB 3,259 to Weihai Overseas Shipping. Prior to this, Huabu Company had requested the customs-released bill of lading for the "Nikolai" from Weihai Overseas Shipping, but Weihai Overseas Shipping refused to return the bill of lading on the grounds that agency fees had not been paid.

On June 2, 1994, the former Timber Company entered into a sale contract with the Ship Scrapping Company, selling the scrap steel ship for RMB 4,971,890 for scrapping.

On June 5, 1994, Weihai Overseas Shipping notified the Weihai Port Authority that the procedures for the ship were complete and it could be released. After the ship departed from port, Weihai Overseas Shipping requested the Weihai Port Authority not to release the ship, claiming that its procedures were incomplete.

On March 12, 1996, the Mudanjiang City Suburban District People's Court of Heilongjiang Province, in hearing the case of *Mudanjiang City Dafeng Agricultural Trade Company (hereinafter referred to as Dafeng Agricultural Trade Company) v. Huabu Company* regarding a canned beef purchase and sale contract dispute, ruled that Huabu Company was liable for breach of contract and ordered it to compensate the plaintiff in that case in the amount of RMB 114,600. That judgment has taken legal effect and has been fully executed.

The facts found and determined by the Shandong High People's Court as above are identical to those found and determined by the Qingdao Maritime Court at the first instance. The Shandong High People's Court also found that the entity that accepted the ship agency appointment from Huabu Company should have been the Weihai Shipping Agency Company, a subsidiary of Weihai Overseas Shipping, but because its registered capital was not fully contributed, it lacked legal person status. Therefore, its civil liability should be borne by its founding entity, Weihai Overseas Shipping.

Based on the above facts, the Shandong High People's Court rendered Civil Judgment No. 236 (1997) Luzhong Zhongzi, dismissing the appeals of Weihai Overseas Shipping and the former Timber Company and affirming Civil Judgment No. 1 (1995) Qinghafa Haishi Chongzi of Qingdao Maritime Court, which held: (1) Weihai Overseas Shipping shall compensate Huabu Company for economic losses of USD 370,600 plus interest on a bank deposit at the same rate from June 8, 1994, until the date of payment determined by this judgment, and RMB 129,600. The former Timber Company shall be jointly and severally liable for such compensation. (2) The former Timber Company shall pay liquidated damages to Huabu Company in the amount of RMB 300,000. After deducting the import customs duties and import value-added tax totaling RMB 232,094.72 paid by the former Timber Company in Huabu Company's name, the final amount of liquidated damages payable shall be RMB 67,905.28.

In its retrial determination, the Shandong High People's Court found: On April 21, 1994, in addition to entering into the two barter trade contracts with the Russian party in the name of Border Trade Company, Huabu Company also entered into two cash trade contracts (one in Chinese and one in Russian) with the same Russian company in its own name, bearing the same contract numbers as the barter trade contracts. The ship price in each was USD 328,000. However, these two contracts were not stamped for record by the Heilongjiang Province Border Trade Administration Bureau.

After the former Timber Company obtained the "Nikolai" ship based on the scrap steel ship purchase and sale agreement it signed with the Russian party, it immediately resold the ship to the Ship Scrapping Company. After the Ship Scrapping Company paid the full ship price, it coordinated with the former Timber Company through the Yantai Port Authority to contact the Weihai Port Authority for the ship's release. The Weihai Port Authority released the ship without conducting a routine inspection. After Weihai Overseas Shipping discovered this, it notified the Port Authority that the ship's procedures were incomplete and should not be released. The Weihai Port Authority then used high-frequency radio to order the ship to stop and await further instructions, but the ship ignored the order.

The retrial ruling of the Shandong High People's Court further determined: During the retrial hearing, the Russian evidence submitted by Huabu Company directly contradicted the evidence submitted by the former Timber Company at the first and second instance trials. However, the Russian evidence submitted by both Huabu Company and the former Timber Company had not been notarized or authenticated by the Chinese embassy in Russia.

The Shandong High People's Court held in its retrial ruling:

(I) After signing the barter trade contracts, Huabu Company also signed cash trade contracts with the Russian party. During the performance of the contracts, many of its actions were inconsistent with the barter trade contracts but consistent with the cash trade contracts. Moreover, in the record of inquiry made by the Russian party when it applied to participate in the litigation at the first instance, the Russian party admitted that its actual transaction with Huabu Company was a cash trade, with the actual transaction amount being USD 447,005. Huabu Company deceived customs, falsely declared the nature and price of the trade, and evaded a substantial amount of customs duties, which is suspected of constituting the crime of smuggling. The former Timber Company, having later learned of Huabu Company's false declaration of trade nature and customs evasion/smuggling, still actively participated in and directly signed an illegal cash sale contract with the Russian party, evaded customs duties, and resold smuggled goods for profit. Its conduct is also suspected of constituting the crime of smuggling. Weihai Overseas Shipping, having also later learned of the illegal activities of Huabu Company and the former Timber Company, still acted as their customs declaration agent, which was also somewhat erroneous. The first and second instance judgments held that the barter trade contracts were legal and valid and the cash trade contracts were invalid, but they failed to clearly determine which type of trade contract was actually performed by the parties. As a result, they objectively protected a series of illegal activities by the parties, which was erroneous and should be corrected.

(II) After accepting the entrustment from Huabu Company, Weihai Overseas Shipping did not intervene in the commercial activities of Huabu Company, the former Timber Company, and the Russian party during the entire agency process. Its actions did not exceed the scope of its duties as a ship agent. Whether the "Nikolai" ship was allowed to leave port was the prerogative of the port authority, and there was no legal causal relationship between Weihai Overseas Shipping's phone call and the release of the ship. The customs-released bill of lading remained in the possession of Weihai Overseas Shipping at all times and was not given to Huabu Company or the former Timber Company. There was no evidence supporting the alleged malicious collusion between Weihai Overseas Shipping and the former Timber Company or the fact that Weihai Overseas Shipping privately released the ship. The first instance judgment's finding that Weihai Overseas Shipping and the former Timber Company maliciously colluded, arbitrarily notified the Weihai Port Authority to release the ship to the former Timber Company, and harmed Huabu Company's interests lacked factual basis. Huabu Company's claims against Weihai Overseas Shipping should be dismissed.

(III) The Russian evidence provided by Huabu Company during the retrial and by the former Timber Company during the first and second instance trials were directly contradictory evidence on the same facts. Neither party had sufficient evidence to disprove the other's evidence. Moreover, the above evidence had not been notarized or authenticated by Chinese embassies or consulates in Russia. This court was unable to verify it and therefore declined to accept it.

(IV) This case is a dispute arising from the sale of a ship. The first and second instance courts characterized the case as a ship agency dispute, which failed to reflect the essence of the case and was an overly narrow characterization. This should be corrected.

The Shandong High People's Court ruled in its retrial: revoking Civil Judgment No. 236 (1997) Luzhong Zhongzi of this court and Civil Judgment No. 1 (1995) Qinghafa Haishi Chongzi of Qingdao Maritime Court; dismissing Huabu Company's lawsuit; and transferring this case to the public security authorities for handling.

Huabu Company, dissatisfied with the retrial ruling of the Shandong High People's Court, applied to this court for a retrial, raising the following reasons:

(I) Huabu Company's claim is a ship agency dispute in which Weihai Overseas Shipping breached the agency agreement, exceeded its authority, and colluded with the former Timber Company, causing substantial economic losses to the principal. The retrial ruling recharacterized the case as a ship sale dispute and further changed the nature of the trade contract between Huabu Company and the Russian party, finding that Huabu Company committed smuggling. This constitutes local protectionism. The retrial ruling's finding that Huabu Company actually performed a cash contract has no factual or legal basis. According to the document Heibianju Maozi (1993) No. 201 formulated by Heilongjiang Province based on the State Council document dated December 15, 1984, Huabu Company entrusted the Border Trade Company, which has import and export rights, to sign barter trade contracts with the Russian party. The contracts actually performed were also barter trade contracts. The barter trade contracts signed through entrustment by Huabu Company are lawful and valid, and Huabu Company's trade conduct was also lawful. The retrial ruling's subjective assumptions and pieced-together finding of so-called cash contracts confuse the facts and violate laws and regulations. The buyer under the alleged cash contract is not Dongning Border Trade Company, and the text was not signed or sealed by Huabu Company's legal person or its then legal representative. The document is merely a Russian-language letter of intent signed personally by Li Wenyi. According to Articles 4 and 6 of the *Supreme People's Court's Answers to Questions Concerning the Application of the Foreign Economic Contract Law*, it is invalid. Furthermore, the text does not contain key details such as the ship's name and tonnage, which would confirm it relates to the same subject matter as the barter trade contract. Based on the legally effective evidence provided by the Russian party, the "Nikolai" ship delivery receipt signed by Qu Shouzhang of Weihai Overseas Shipping on behalf of Huabu Company (which states "in accordance with the provisions of Barter Trade Contract No. HLDO-1206 dated April 21, 1994"), the commercial invoice issued by the Russian party, the evidence of the canned beef purchase contract Huabu Company signed with a domestic supplier to perform the barter trade contract, and the fact that Huabu Company did not pay a single cent of the ship price to the Russian party, other than USD 30,000 for the crew's repatriation fees and USD 100,000 in intermediary fees to an intermediary company, all these prove that Huabu Company signed and performed a barter trade contract.

(II) The retrial ruling found that Huabu Company participated in the ship handover procedures. However, Weihai Overseas Shipping and the former Timber Company admitted that Huabu Company did not participate in the handover procedures with the Russian party. The facts are: No one from Huabu Company boarded the ship on May 9; on May 17, Weihai Overseas Shipping, behind Huabu Company's back, conspired with the former Timber Company to complete the handover procedures with the Russian party and privately delivered the "Nikolai" ship to the former Timber Company. The facts demonstrating the collusion between Weihai Overseas Shipping and the former Timber Company are: (1) When handling import procedures on behalf of Huabu Company, Weihai Overseas Shipping, behind Huabu Company's back, led personnel from the former Timber Company to handle the procedures and submitted the ship sale agreement between Huabu Company and the former Timber Company to the relevant authorities, leading them to mistakenly believe that the ship was imported by the former Timber Company. This laid the foundation for the former Timber Company to surreptitiously tow away the "Nikolai" ship. (2) After completing customs declaration on behalf of Huabu Company on May 7, 1994, Weihai Overseas Shipping handed over Huabu Company's original contracts and the ship's documents retrieved from the "Nikolai" to the former Timber Company. (3) One year after this lawsuit was filed, Weihai Overseas Shipping produced a bill of lading with the consignee listed as Weihai Overseas Shipping. (4) Weihai Overseas Shipping declared that after May 9, 1994, it terminated its agency relationship with Huabu Company and became the agent for the former Timber Company. (5) Weihai Overseas Shipping, behind Huabu Company's back, conspired with the former Timber Company to complete the ship handover procedures with the Russian party and delivered the ship to the former Timber Company. (6) On June 2, 1994, when Huabu Company requested the bill of lading from Weihai Overseas Shipping, Weihai Overseas Shipping refused to return it on the grounds that agency fees had not been paid, claiming that the former Timber Company had paid the fees. In fact, the former Timber Company only paid the fees on June 8. (7) On June 5, Qu Shouzhang of Weihai Overseas Shipping telephoned the Port Authority, stating that the procedures were complete and the ship could be released, thereby enabling the former Timber Company to successfully tow the ship away.

(III) The Russian evidence provided by Huabu Company was notarized by a Russian notary public. The retrial ruling's finding that it was not notarized conceals the facts to deny its legal effect. The ruling's refusal to accept the evidence from either party in effect denies Huabu Company's valid evidence.

Weihai Overseas Shipping and the former Timber Company did not submit a defense within the defense period. Weihai Overseas Shipping argued at the hearing:

(I) Huabu Company did not obtain any lawful rights or interests in the scrap steel ship and therefore lacks standing to sue Weihai Overseas Shipping. Simultaneously with signing the barter trade contract with the Russian party, Huabu Company also signed a cash trade contract bearing the same contract number. Huabu Company's representative actually paid USD 130,000 in cash to the Russian party and issued a "Letter of Guarantee" for payment. Only after the former Timber Company paid the remaining ship price did the Russian party deliver the ship. This indicates that the actual performance was a cash trade. Huabu Company is a shell company with registered capital of only RMB 300,000. It deceived customs by using the barter trade contract to obtain a 50% reduction in import duties but had no ability to perform the barter trade contract. Huabu Company's transfer of its contractual rights and interests to the Timber Company was its true intention. Huabu Company has no rights or interests whatsoever in the subject matter of the barter trade contract in this case, and naturally has no ownership of the scrap steel ship and, consequently, no standing to sue.

(II) The former Timber Company is the true rights holder under the trade contract in this case. There was no error in the delivery of the ship. The former Timber Company's acceptance of the ship was determined by its contract with Huabu Company and the fact that Huabu Company and the Russian party could not perform their contract. There was no delivery error. Weihai Overseas Shipping carried out the joint inspection and other ship handover procedures at the request of Huabu Company, the Russian party, and the former Timber Company, and there was no fault or malicious collusion on its part.

(3) Weihai Foreign Transport properly performed the agency contract with Huabu Company. The subject matter of this case was an imported scrap steel vessel. The agency business entrusted by Huabu Company to Weihai Foreign Transport had the dual nature of both ship agency business and cargo agency business, including ship agency tasks such as joint vessel inspection and crew handover, as well as cargo agency tasks such as declaring the vessel as imported cargo for customs clearance. As a cargo agent, Weihai Foreign Transport should have delivered the customs-cleared bill of lading to Huabu Company, but as a ship agent, it was required by customs to retain the original customs clearance release order for inspection. Weihai Foreign Transport discovered that the bill of lading submitted by Huabu Company did not bear the Russian party's signature and requested Huabu Company to provide a compliant original bill of lading. The bill of lading in this case did not possess "property right attributes"; the Russian party delivered the vessel upon receipt of payment and cash receipt. Thus, it is understandable why Huabu Company held the bill of lading before fully paying the vessel price, why the Russian party issued a second set of bills of lading to the Original Timber Company after it paid the full vessel price, and why a third set of bills of lading was issued to Huabu Company four years later. Weihai Foreign Transport was entirely correct in not releasing the bill of lading to Huabu Company, which had not paid any portion of the vessel price. After learning that the Original Timber Company had towed the vessel out of Weihai Port without the approval of Weihai Port Supervisory Authority, Weihai Foreign Transport notified the Authority that the vessel's release procedures were incomplete and that it could not be released. Huabu Company's claim that Weihai Foreign Transport instructed the Port Supervisory Authority to release the vessel is unfounded. Weihai Foreign Transport discovered that Huabu Company was actually performing a cash trade, but considering that Huabu Company had already paid USD 130,000, it continued to perform the agency contract to protect the interests of the Chinese side.

(4) This case involves suspected smuggling crimes by using barter trade as a pretext to carry out cash trade and evade customs duties, with multiple parties and individuals suspected of joint criminal offenses. We request the court and relevant authorities to investigate and pursue the criminal liability of the suspected criminals in accordance with the law.

Evidence materials submitted by Huabu Company to the court include:

1. Contracts for the import of scrap steel vessel and steel wire rod, and export of canned beef, both under contract number HLDO-1206, along with vessel invoices and delivery invoices, to prove the existence of the barter trade contract.
2. The authorization certificate for entrusted agency approved by the Heilongjiang Provincial Border Trade Bureau, Document No. [1993] 201 of the Heilongjiang Provincial Border Trade Bureau, and Document No. (1994) 014 of the Dongning County Border Trade Bureau, to prove that the barter trade contract was lawful and valid.
3. A judgment concerning a contract dispute over the purchase of canned beef and a settlement agreement for execution, to prove that Huabu Company carried out domestic procurement of goods to fulfill the barter trade contract.
4. Customs declarations, to prove that Weihai Foreign Transport, as agent, declared import of the scrap steel vessel under the barter trade contract.
5. A customs-cleared order bill of lading, bearing the release stamps of both Russian customs and Chinese customs, to prove that the bill of lading was valid and that the vessel, as imported goods, should be delivered to Huabu Company.
6. An application for the import of an international navigation vessel (a copy extracted from the Second Section of Customs Supervision), to prove that Weihai Foreign Transport applied for vessel import on behalf of Huabu Company.
7. Special payment receipts for import duties and import value-added tax, to prove that the taxpayer was Heilongjiang Dongning Border Economic and Trade Company, which handled import agency for Huabu Company.
8. Invoices from Weihai Foreign Transport, to prove that Weihai Foreign Transport received agency fees paid by the Original Timber Company on behalf of Huabu Company.
9. A notarized certificate from Russian Captain Nikolsky dated September 5, 1997, to prove the use of the USD 130,000 paid by Huabu Company, of which USD 100,000 was paid as intermediary service fees and USD 30,000 as expenses for the ship crew, and not as vessel price.
10. A certificate signed by Russian General Manager Dechik, to prove that the Russian party's delivery was in fulfillment of the barter contract HLDO-1206, and that, in accordance with the "General Conditions for Delivery of Goods between China and the Soviet Union" and Article 15 of the contract, ownership of the vessel had been transferred to Huabu Company on April 26, 1994.
11. The original order bill of lading issued by the Russian party on April 26, 1994, and certificates from Nikolsky and Dechik, to prove the source of a valid original bill of lading subsequently provided to Huabu Company, that the order bill of lading originally given to Huabu Company for customs declaration was consistent with the original bill of lading retained by the Russian company, and that the consignee on the bill of lading was Huabu Company.
12. A notarized certificate from Russian Captain Nikolsky dated September 5, 1997, to prove that on May 7, 1994, Weihai Foreign Transport, in the name of Huabu Company, obtained from the captain all vessel documents and the vessel deletion certificate for the M/V "Nikolai".
13. A copy of the "Certificate of Deletion of Vessel Registration from the Russian Maritime Register of Shipping" certified as authentic by the Supervisory Officer of the Primorsky Regional Registration Office of the Russian Maritime Register of Shipping, to prove that the M/V "Nikolai" was deleted from registration at Nakhodka Fishing Port on April 24, 1994, due to the HLDO-1206 contract between the Russian party and Huabu Company.
14. A certificate signed by the Supervisory Officer of the Russian Maritime Register of Shipping, to prove that, in accordance with the HLDO-1206 contract, the Register issued a one-time navigation permit for the M/V "Nikolai" to Dalian Port on April 25, 1994.
15. A fax copy of an order from the Russian Far East Fishing Joint-Stock Company, to prove that the company had sold the M/V "Nikolai" as a scrap steel vessel to Huabu Company in accordance with the contract.
16. A vessel delivery note, to prove that the Russian party delivered the vessel on May 17, 1994, and that the delivery was made to Huabu Company under the barter contract HLDO-1206 dated April 21, 1994, with Qu Shouzhang of Weihai Foreign Transport signing on the consignee side.
17. A notarized certificate from Russian Captain Nikolsky dated September 5, 1997, to prove that when the Russian party delivered the vessel to Huabu Company on May 17, 1994, it asked why no one from Huabu Company was present, and Qu Shouzhang of Weihai Foreign Transport stated that he fully represented Huabu Company.
18. A notarized certificate from Russian Captain Nikolsky dated September 5, 1997, concerning a guarantee, to prove that Li Wenyi never made any guarantee on behalf of Huabu Company that violated the barter trade contract, and to prove that it was Weihai Foreign Transport and the Original Timber Company who repeatedly requested the Russian party to sell the vessel directly to the Original Timber Company in cash trade and to pressure Huabu Company to change the barter trade to cash trade.
19. Testimonies from Russian Captain Nikolsky and Dechik, General Manager of the South Sea Fishing Fleet Joint-Stock Company, to prove the circumstances under which the Russian party, deceived, signed a cash purchase agreement with the Original Timber Company on May 13, 1994, and that the date May 17 was altered by the Original Timber Company. The Russian party declares that the agreement is null and void.
20. An order bill of lading issued by the Russian party to the Original Timber Company, to prove the malicious breach of contract by Weihai Foreign Transport and the Original Timber Company.
21. Four credit slips from the Weihai Economic and Technological Development Zone Sub-branch of the Bank of China, to prove that the Original Timber Company colluded with the bank to issue false remittance documents.
22. Certification materials from the Heilongjiang Provincial Tobacco Corporation regarding "President Xu" and "President Bai", to prove that the testimonies of Weihai Foreign Transport and the Original Timber Company regarding "President Bai" were fabricated and false.
23. General Conditions for Delivery of Goods between China and the Soviet Union.

Weihai Foreign Transport submitted to the court a list of 35 items of evidence, of which the evidence submitted by Weihai Foreign Transport includes:

1. A cash purchase vessel contract signed between Huabu Company and the Russian party on April 21, 1994, and a supplementary agreement to the cash purchase vessel contract signed between Huabu Company and the Russian party on April 22, 1994, to prove that the actual contract signed between Huabu Company and the Russian party was a cash trade contract.
2. A payment guarantee written by Li Wenyi of Huabu Company to the Russian party, to prove that Huabu Company guaranteed performance of the cash trade.
3. A cash purchase vessel agreement signed between the Original Timber Company and the Russian party, to prove that the Russian party delivered the vessel in accordance with the cash trade contract with the Original Timber Company.
4. A letter from Russian representative Slava to the Shandong High People's Court, to prove that the transaction was a cash trade.
5. A "Supplementary Explanation of Facts" submitted by the Original Timber Company to the court.
6. A certificate of cash purchase of the vessel by the Russian party, to prove the existence and performance of the cash trade contract.
7. A certificate from Russian representative Slava regarding the retrieval of archival materials from the vessel, to prove that the Russian party performed the cash purchase contract.
8. A receipt issued by Li Wenyi of Huabu Company to the Original Timber Company for payment received, to prove that Li Wenyi borrowed money from the Original Timber Company and that Huabu Company was unable to perform the trade contract with the Russian party.
9. A customs-cleared bill of lading, to prove that the bill of lading was invalid for lack of the Russian party's signature.
10. The full-day duty log of the Weihai Port Supervisory Authority dated June 5, 1994, and evidence provided by the Weihai Port Supervisory Authority duty room, to prove that Weihai Foreign Transport did not instruct the Port Supervisory Authority to release the vessel.
11. An agency fee receipt, to prove that the agency fee was paid by the Original Timber Company, and that Huabu Company did not pay the agency fee.
12. An original order bill of lading issued by the Russian party to the Original Timber Company, to prove that the Russian party sold the vessel to the Original Timber Company. Weihai Foreign Transport challenged Huabu Company's evidence, stating: There is no objection to the recordal of the barter trade contract between Huabu Company and Russia with the Border Trade Bureau, but the barter trade contract was formally defective and was never actually performed; Huabu Company and the Russian party also had an unregistered cash trade contract, with a guarantee written by Li Wenyi himself promising payment; the Russian party's evidentiary documents are contradictory to the evidence initially provided, and under international practice, such evidence should be notarized and authenticated before being used as evidence; they questioned the source of the credit slips from the Weihai Economic and Technological Development Zone Sub-branch of the Bank of China, and further stated that this evidence could not prove collusion between Weihai Foreign Transport and the bank. Huabu Company rebutted Weihai Foreign Transport's challenges, stating: The evidentiary documents submitted by Huabu Company from the Russian party were notarized and, in accordance with the provisions of the bilateral treaty on judicial assistance between China and Russia, should be valid evidence; conversely, the so-called Russian evidence provided by the opposing party did not comply with the bilateral treaty; the credit slips were provided to Huabu Company by the Russian party after the second instance trial.

Huabu Company challenged Weihai Foreign Transport's evidence, stating: Regarding evidence 1, it acknowledged the objective existence of the cash trade contract and supplementary agreement, but these contract documents had not taken effect and thus had no legal force, and were irrelevant to this case; regarding evidence 2, the "Guarantee" lacked essential content, and Huabu Company was unaware of the content added later by Weihai Foreign Transport, so the guarantee had no legal effect; regarding evidence 5, it only proved that Weihai Foreign Transport knew the Original Timber Company was engaging in a cash trade; regarding evidence 4, 6, and 7, they contradicted the notarized Russian evidence and had been denied by the Russian party, and should not be accepted; regarding evidence 8, it objectively existed, but was a receipt for payment received rather than an IOU; regarding evidence 9, there was no objection to its authenticity, but the bill of lading had been stamped for customs clearance and, although unsigned, this did not affect its legal validity; regarding evidence 10 and 11, no objections; regarding evidence 12, the bill of lading did not bear the Russian customs export release stamp and did not meet requirements. Weihai Foreign Transport rebutted Huabu Company's challenges, stating: The matters guaranteed in the guarantee had been performed; the Russian party's certificates were written by the parties in China and did not require notarization; the presence or absence of an export customs release stamp from the exporting country was not a requirement for a bill of lading.

After hearing the evidence during the court session, this court finds: The facts that Huabu Company and the Original Timber Company entered into a contract for the sale of the scrap steel vessel M/V "Nikolai", and that Huabu Company and Weihai Foreign Transport entered into an agency contract, are supported by documentary evidence including the agreements, supplementary agreements, and powers of attorney. The parties do not deny these facts, and this court affirms them. In accordance with Article 29 of the Treaty between the People's Republic of China and the Russian Federation on Judicial Assistance in Civil and Criminal Matters, official documents produced within the territory of Russia, or documents produced or certified by Russian courts or competent authorities, are valid as long as they are signed and officially sealed. The documents signed by the Russian Maritime Register of Shipping and the documents signed and certified by a notary in this case are accepted by this court as evidence. The objections and challenges raised by Weihai Foreign Transport in this regard are not supported by this court. Weihai Foreign Transport questioned the source of the bank credit slips but did not provide counter-evidence to negate their objectivity. During the first instance trial, the Original Timber Company already admitted that it had remitted the vessel price to a "special account" opened in Weihai City in the name of the Russian vessel company, and later transferred the funds to its own account. This can prove that the "special account" did indeed receive this credit, and the authenticity of the credit slip is affirmed by this court. The text of the cash trade contract submitted by Weihai Foreign Transport objectively exists, but this contract was not approved by the relevant local border trade administration authority in Heilongjiang and was not recognized by the relevant parties. Therefore, it cannot be deemed a valid contract, and the relevant materials should not be used as evidence in this case. This court does not accept them. As for the guarantee submitted by Weihai Foreign Transport, both Huabu Company and the Russian party have denied it, and this court does not accept the guarantee. Other evidence and facts that the parties do not object to are all accepted by this court. Accordingly, this court finds the following facts:

Huabu Company, with the approval of the competent authority, entrusted a border trade company to sign a barter trade contract with the Russian Primorsky Company for the import of a scrap steel vessel and steel wire rod, and the export of canned beef. The contract stipulated that the scrap steel vessel and steel wire rod, among other items, would be delivered in May of the same year, and that the canned beef would be delivered within 1994. The contract was stamped and filed with the Heilongjiang Provincial Border Trade Administration Bureau and was approved by the People's Republic of China Dongning Customs to apply a reduced tariff rate of 50% for the import of the scrap steel vessel under barter trade. To fulfill its delivery obligation, the Russian Primorsky Company had already registered the deletion of the M/V "Nikolai" on April 24, 1994, and transferred ownership to Huabu Company on April 26, 1994, in accordance with the contract. To perform the barter trade contract, Huabu Company signed a contract with a domestic supplier for the purchase of canned beef of equivalent value.

The facts that Huabu Company and the Original Timber Company entered into a scrap steel vessel sale agreement (contract) and a compensation agreement, and that Huabu Company and Weihai Foreign Transport entered into an agency contract, are consistent with the facts found in the Shandong High People's Court's original final judgment in this case.

On May 4, 1994, Weihai Foreign Transport declared the import of the M/V "Nikolai" to the Weihai Port Supervisory Authority; on May 7, Weihai Foreign Transport, in the name of Huabu Company, took possession from the captain of the M/V "Nikolai" of all vessel documents and the vessel deletion certificate issued by the competent Russian authority, and on the same day declared the M/V "Nikolai" as cargo for import to the customs. Subsequently, on June 2, Huabu Company demanded from Weihai Foreign Transport the bill of lading and import vessel documents, but Weihai Foreign Transport refused on the grounds that Huabu Company had not paid the agency fees.

On April 30 of the same year, the Original Timber Company paid Huabu Company a deposit of RMB 300,000 for the vessel purchase, and on May 6 and 7 paid a total of USD 100,000 as partial payment for the vessel.

On May 13 of the same year, the Original Timber Company signed an agreement with the Russian Vessel Company for the sale and purchase of the scrap steel vessel M/V "Nikolai", stipulating the resale of the vessel to the Original Timber Company. The Original Timber Company changed the date of this agreement to May 17.

On May 17 of the same year, Weihai Foreign Transport, without the participation or knowledge of Huabu Company, together with the Original Timber Company, completed the handover of the vessel and crew for the M/V "Nikolai" with the Russian personnel on board. Qu Shouzhang of Weihai Foreign Transport signed on the consignee side of the delivery note.

On June 1 of the same year, after collecting the import duties and import value-added tax paid by the Original Timber Company in the name of Dongning Border Trade Company, Weihai Customs stamped the order bill of lading submitted for customs declaration with a release seal, authorizing its release.

On June 2 of the same year, the Original Timber Company signed a sale contract with a shipbreaking company to sell the scrap steel vessel M/V "Nikolai" to the shipbreaking company for dismantling at a price of RMB 4,971,890.

On June 8 of the same year, the Original Timber Company paid Weihai Foreign Transport agency fees of RMB 3,259.

This court holds that this case is a dispute over a vessel import agency contract and a domestic scrap steel vessel sale contract arising from the agency contract between Huabu Company and Weihai Foreign Transport, and the vessel sale contract between Huabu Company and the Original Timber Company. The parties and the contract facts are all within the territory of the People's Republic of China. Therefore, the laws of the People's Republic of China should apply to this case. The vessel involved in this case was imported from the Russian Federation (hereinafter "Russia"), and some evidence originates from Russia. The transfer of ownership of the vessel and the validity of evidence originating from Russia should be governed by the bilateral treaty between the People's Republic of China and Russia. The barter trade contract signed by Huabu Company through its border trade agent with the Russian Primorsky Company for the import of a scrap steel vessel and steel wire rod, and the export of canned beef, was approved by the Border Trade Administration Bureau and approved by Dongning Customs for a reduced tariff rate of 50%. It is a lawful and valid contract. The contract for the sale of canned beef signed by Huabu Company with the domestic supplier Dafeng Agriculture and Trade Company, and the subsequent request by the Russian party for Huabu Company to continue performing the contract by delivering canned beef, serve as circumstantial evidence of the performance of the barter trade contract. This case is not a trade contract dispute between Huabu Company and the Russian Primorsky Company, and according to the arbitration clause in that contract, the Shandong High People's Court does not have jurisdiction over that contract. Therefore, the original retrial ruling of that court, which recharacterized the nature of this case as a sale contract dispute and focused on whether the sale contract between the Chinese and Russian parties was performed properly, was inappropriate. The notarized documents issued by the Russian party confirm that the contract signed and performed with Huabu Company was a barter trade contract. When the M/V "Nikolai" departed from a Russian port to sail to Dalian Port, China, for delivery, the vessel's ownership had already been deleted from the Russian Maritime Register of Shipping. In accordance with the provisions of the bilateral trade agreement between China and Russia, ownership of the vessel had already been transferred to Huabu Company. After the M/V "Nikolai" arrived at Dalian Port, at the request of the Original Timber Company, the Russian party sailed the vessel to Weihai Port for delivery. This inevitably created or incurred additional transport obligations and risks, including the consumption of fuel and fresh water. Pursuant to the agreement, the Chinese side paid the above expenses to the Russian crew and the Russian Vessel Company. Such payment does not constitute payment of the vessel price to the Russian Primorsky Company and should not be included in the price of the scrap steel vessel. The retrial of the Shandong High People's Court held that a cash trade contract actually existed between Huabu Company and the Russian party. However, apart from the verifiable payment of USD 130,000 to the Russian crew and the Russian Vessel Company, there is no evidence proving that Huabu Company paid the vessel price in cash to the Russian Primorsky Company. The original retrial ruling of the Shandong High People's Court finding that Huabu Company and the Russian party actually performed a cash trade contract lacks sufficient evidence. The presumption that Huabu Company used the barter trade contract as a pretext to conceal a cash trade, thereby constituting suspected smuggling, was improper.

Weihai Ocean Shipping, as the ship agent and import cargo agent of Huabu Company, accepted from its principal all the documents required for import customs declaration, including the barter trade contract, certificate of approval for tariff reduction/exemption, bill of lading, and other documents, and was obligated to perform all entrusted matters of ship agency and handling of cargo import procedures. Upon completion of various procedures or when the principal requested the return of relevant documents, it was required to return all documents except those that should be retained by customs, port supervision, and other relevant authorities according to law. When an agent performs its agency obligations, maintaining the legitimate rights and interests of the principal is its implied basic duty. After Weihai Ocean Shipping obtained from the Russian captain the ship documents of the "Nikolay" and the documents evidencing deregistration of ship registry, it neither acted as agent for Huabu Company to handle ship registration procedures at the ship registration authority nor returned the relevant documents to Huabu Company for handling ship registration; its inaction damaged the legitimate rights and interests of Huabu Company. Weihai Ocean Shipping's demand that Huabu Company pay agency fees was its legitimate right, but its refusal to return to Huabu Company the bill of lading released with customs seal and the complete set of documents of the barter trade contract, the ship documents of the "Nikolay," and the documents evidencing deregistration of ship registry on the grounds that Huabu Company had not paid the agency fees, and its delivery of the aforementioned documents other than the bill of lading to Yuanmu Timber Company, constituted a breach of the agency contract, and it shall bear the damages resulting therefrom. When Weihai Ocean Shipping clearly knew that the ship was imported by Huabu Company, it refused to deliver the relevant documents, failed to notify Huabu Company to be present on site, but instead, together with Yuanmu Timber Company, handled the ship delivery procedures with the Russian side, delivered the "Nikolay" ship to the Chinese crew members appointed by Yuanmu Timber Company for management, thereby effectively placing it under the control of Yuanmu Timber Company, which gave Yuanmu Timber Company the opportunity to tow the ship out of Weihai Port. Weihai Ocean Shipping shall also bear corresponding liability for this.

Apart from bearing corresponding contractual obligations pursuant to their respective contracts with Huabu Company, Weihai Ocean Shipping and Yuanmu Timber Company shall also bear implied obligations, namely, to respect the rights of Huabu Company over the imported "Nikolay" ship. Yuanmu Timber Company, as the buyer in the domestic scrap steel vessel sales contract with Huabu Company, clearly knew that the seller Huabu Company had acquired ownership of the "Nikolay" ship imported from Russia through an international trade contract and resold it to itself, and obtained from Weihai Ocean Shipping the ship documents including the documents evidencing deregistration of ship registry. Its failure to pay the ship price to Huabu Company already constituted a breach of contract, and it shall bear liability for breach of contract. Yuanmu Timber Company also entered into a "scrap steel vessel sales contract" for the "Nikolay" with the ship personnel of the Russian Fleet Company, which had already deregistered the Russian registry of the "Nikolay" and lost ownership of the ship; this constituted malicious conduct, and such "contract" has no legal effect. Yuanmu Timber Company shall bear corresponding civil liability for the consequences arising therefrom and the losses caused to Huabu Company. Weihai Ocean Shipping, as the ship and cargo agent for Huabu Company's import of the "Nikolay" ship, clearly knew that Huabu Company had lawfully acquired ownership of the "Nikolay" through the trade contract. Before Yuanmu Timber Company and the Russian Fleet Company illegally entered into the contract, Weihai Ocean Shipping had already obtained the ship documents of the "Nikolay" and learned that the Russian side had deregistered the ship's registry. In its subsequent agency conduct, it recognized such illegal contract, repeatedly protected the improper interests of Yuanmu Timber Company, successively delivered the ship documents and the ship itself to Yuanmu Timber Company, thereby damaging the legitimate rights and interests of its principal. The facts constituting malicious collusion with Yuanmu Timber Company have been established. Pursuant to Article 66, paragraphs 2 and 3 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the PRC, it shall bear joint and several civil liability for damages with Yuanmu Timber Company.

This Court is of the opinion that the retrial ruling of the Shandong High People's Court found insufficient grounds for the determination that the parties involved in this case were suspected of crimes. Even if the persons involved are suspected of crimes, this does not affect Huabu Company's right to protect its legitimate rights and interests based on lawful and valid contractual legal relationships and to file a lawsuit against Weihai Ocean Shipping and Yuanmu Timber Company. Pursuant to Article 1 of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Trial of Economic Dispute Cases Involving Suspected Economic Crimes, which states, "If the same citizen, legal person, or other economic organization is involved in an economic dispute and suspected economic crime based on different legal facts, the economic dispute case and the economic crime suspect case shall be tried separately," the people's court may still try the civil dispute in this case. The retrial ruling of the court of first instance erroneously applied the law, improperly dismissed Huabu Company's lawsuit, and improperly transferred the entire case to the public security organ. Although the Civil Judgment No. 236 (1997) Lu Jing Zhong Zi of that court failed to find certain facts of this case and found certain facts inadequately, the basic facts were clearly found, the law was correctly applied, and the judgment result was appropriate, and it shall be affirmed. Accordingly, the ruling is as follows:

1. Civil Ruling No. 167 (1997) Lu Jing Zai Zi of the Shandong High People's Court is hereby vacated;

2. Civil Judgment No. 236 (1997) Lu Jing Zhong Zi of the Shandong High People's Court is hereby affirmed.

This ruling is final.
